input_signals.name: ProfitGatedNetPayout
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), 0), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvc), sstk), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net payout is a credible signal of undervalued cash generation only when the firm has sustained positive operating income; distributions by unprofitable firms carry no information (or reflect liquidation of assets).
input_signals.reasoning: The indicator gates the industry-standardized net equity payout on three-year positive operating profitability, switching the financing signal off exactly where its economic story breaks down. This conditional structure should sharpen the payout premium relative to an unconditional payout sort and produce a cleaner long leg of profitable distributors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ), 0 ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( add( prstkc, dvc ), sstk ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: DistributionCapacityUtilization
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), ADD(sstk, dltis)), MAX(oancf, dp)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Scaling net distributions by the firm's own internally generated funds measures how much of its cash-generating capacity management is willing to hand back; high utilization signals confident, underpriced cash flow while negative utilization signals external dependence.
input_signals.reasoning: The denominator MAX(oancf, dp) is a floor-protected measure of internal cash generation, making the ratio a direct profitability-financing intensity rather than an asset-scaled flow. Firms distributing a large share of self-generated cash reveal durable operating strength, whereas firms whose issuance exceeds internal funds are systematically over-extrapolated by investors.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( add( prstkc, dvt ), add( sstk, dltis ) ), max( oancf, dp ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: ProfitableNetEquityInjection
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(DELTA(ceq, 1), dvt), ib), at), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net equity injected from outside the firm (book equity growth not explained by retained earnings) is a market-timing signal chiefly when the firm is already highly profitable and therefore has no funding necessity; such firms are exploiting a rich valuation of their earnings stream.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg is now a clean accounting identity residual, DELTA(ceq) plus dividends minus income scaled by assets, which is immune to splits and stock dividends that contaminated raw share-count growth. The industry rank of smoothed operating profitability acts as a bounded non-negative weight, so the signal attenuates dilution by distressed firms and concentrates the short leg on unnecessary issuance by strong operators — an asymmetry the plain issuance factor cannot express.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), winsor( ratio( sub( add( delta( ceq, 1 ), dvt ), ib ), at ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: CashProfitPayoutConjunction
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(prstkc, SUB(at, at)), dvt), sstk), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Underpriced cash generation requires both legs simultaneously: sustained cash-based operating profitability and net return of capital to shareholders; a firm strong on only one leg (cash-rich hoarder, or payer without cash generation) carries no comparable premium.
input_signals.reasoning: MIN of two industry ranks implements the conjunction the earlier SUMRANK version only claimed, and unlike an indicator gate it is continuous, so the extreme portfolios remain well populated rather than being swamped by a mass point at zero. Cash-flow-based profitability (oancf) and cash-flow-statement payout are chosen because neither is a linear proxy for CMA or RMW, addressing the FF5-spanning problem seen in ProfitableNetEquityInjection; missing prstkc is set to zero because non-reporting firms did not repurchase.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( coalesce( prstkc, sub( at, at ) ), dvt ), sstk ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: PersistentProfitableRepurchaser
input_signals.expression: TS_SUM(MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(ib, at), 0), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, sstk), at), 0)), 5)
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters is not a single year's coincidence of profit and buyback but the number of years out of five in which the firm was both profitable and a net equity retirer; repeated joint occurrence signals a management team with credible, self-funded cash flow that the market extrapolates too slowly.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests persistence of the interaction itself, a state concept that no level or change specification can express, and it produces a coarse 0–5 score whose extreme buckets are large and stable — a direct remedy for the unstable portfolio composition of the gated payout signal. It also cannot be replicated by either single-theme anomaly, since a firm can be persistently profitable without ever retiring equity and vice versa.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ts_sum( mul( indicator( ratio( ib, at ), 0 ), indicator( ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), at ), 0 ) ), 5 )

input_signals.name: ProfitWeightedExternalFinancing
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Conditional on being operationally strong, the direction of a firm's external capital flow is a valuation signal: profitable firms raising equity and debt are timing rich prices or hiding a funding need and underperform, while profitable firms retiring equity and debt are underpriced cash generators.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing MIN with a signed product fixes the tail problem the critic identified: the profitability rank is a bounded non-negative amplifier, so the short leg is profitable heavy financers and the long leg is profitable heavy distributors, while unprofitable firms are compressed toward zero in the middle instead of contaminating an extreme portfolio. Relative to gen-0's ProfitableNetEquityInjection, the financing leg is built from cash-flow-statement issuance and retirement flows rather than DELTA(ceq), which was essentially asset growth and therefore absorbed by the FF5 investment factor (positive alpha despite fmb = −3.34).
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitBackedPayoutIncrease
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvt), at), 1), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: An increase in distributions is credible information about underpriced cash generation only when the firm has an established operating profit base to fund it; the same payout increase by a weak operator is a liquidation or signalling gamble and carries no premium.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the payout-ratio family the critic flagged as a smoothing variant and tests a different economic event — the change in distribution policy — with operating profitability entering as the conditioning strength that makes the change credible. Scaling by assets removes the near-zero MAX(oibdp, dp) denominator entirely and imposes only a one-year history requirement, so coverage should exceed the 0.079 of the archive's ratio while the interaction (payout *news* × profit *base*) is not reproducible from either theme alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), winsor( delta( ratio( add( prstkc, dvt ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitabilityWithFinancingSwing
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that is already profitable and has just swung from external funding toward net capital return is signalling that internally generated cash now exceeds its needs; the swing, rather than the level of net financing, is the news the market is slow to price.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg is the year-over-year *change* in net external financing, so this is not the published net-external-financing level anomaly, and the rank-composite structure is the one that produced the archive's best FF5 alpha (t = 2.21). Pairing a state (three-year profitability) with a flow-direction change also tests whether the interaction operates through financing news rather than financing status.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ), neg( delta( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitableBuybackTilt
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(prstkc, dvc), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among cash-generative firms, the *composition* of payout is informative: managers who choose repurchases over dividends are acting on a belief that their own equity is cheap, whereas cash-rich firms defaulting to dividends signal no such valuation view.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal treats payout as a single aggregate; this one holds total distribution roughly aside and interacts cash profitability with the repurchase-minus-dividend mix, a genuinely different economic content (managerial valuation signalling versus commitment). Both legs are rank-based so the tails are populated and stable, addressing the portfolio-side weakness of the earlier payout signals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), ind_zscore( ind_rank( ratio( sub( prstkc, dvc ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RolloverBurdenPerCashFlow
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, MAX(oancf, dp)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Short-term debt is only dangerous relative to the cash the business actually generates; firms whose current debt obligations are large multiples of internal cash generation carry refinancing risk that the market systematically underprices.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the financing-deficit/asset-growth family entirely and instead expresses the interaction as a maturity-structure burden deflated by operating cash generation, so identical debt levels score very differently for cash-rich and cash-poor firms. It is unrelated to CMA (no expansion term) and unrelated to RMW (profitability enters only as a deflator), so a surviving FF5 alpha would be new information.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( dlc, max( oancf, dp ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: UnbrokenProfitPayoutConjunction
input_signals.expression: TS_MIN(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(prstkc, dvt), sstk), at), 1))), 4)
input_signals.hypothesis: What identifies durable underpriced cash generation is the absence of any year in which the joint condition broke down: a firm that was in every one of the last four years simultaneously in the upper part of the profitability distribution and a net returner of capital has demonstrably self-funding cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: Taking the time-series minimum of a cross-sectional weakest-link conjunction keeps the profitability leg genuinely binding — a firm with huge payout but mediocre margins scores low, so the expression cannot collapse to a reweighted payout as the critic noted for the MA version. It also fixes the real defect of PersistentProfitableRepurchaser, whose 0–5 integer count produced degenerate mature-firm versus distress buckets, by delivering a continuous rank-valued score with stable membership.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ts_min( min( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( prstkc, dvt ), sstk ), at ), 1 ) ) ), 4 )

input_signals.name: NearTermClaimsCoverageGap
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dlc, dvt), oancf), at), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: What the market underprices is the shortfall between the cash claims a firm must satisfy in the coming year — maturing short-term debt plus its dividend commitment — and the cash its operations produce; a positive gap forces refinancing or a payout cut.
input_signals.reasoning: This expresses the same claims-versus-capacity economics as the winning signal but as an asset-scaled *difference* rather than a *multiple*, which removes the MAX(oancf, dp) floor the critic warned could be near zero, so it separates real economics from denominator artefacts. Adding the dividend commitment to the claims side is a substantive extension: it makes payout enter as an obligation rather than as a reward, which is the opposite role from every payout signal in the archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( sub( add( dlc, dvt ), oancf ), at ), 1 )

input_signals.name: CashBurningIssuer
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))), IND_RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The overvaluation half of the story is concentrated in firms that both burn operating cash and raise equity: issuance funded by necessity rather than opportunity marks firms whose valuations embed growth the cash flows do not support.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior tests used profit levels, profit volatility and interest burden as the conditioner; using the *sign and size of cash burn* is a distinct funding-need channel, and the weakest-link MIN makes the short leg sharp — only firms failing on both dimensions score high — while the long leg contains benign firms that are either cash-generative or non-issuing. This is the appropriate use of MIN for a negative expected sign, since here the diffuse tail is the economically unambiguous one.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExternalFundingShare
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(ADD(sstk, dltis), MAX(oancf, dp))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: The informative quantity is the composition of a firm's cash inflows: when most of the cash entering the firm comes from lenders and new shareholders rather than from operations, the business is dependent on capital-market sentiment, and such dependence is systematically overpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: This is an inflow-*mix* share bounded in [0,1], a structurally different object from the archive's obligation-versus-capacity ratios and differences: it says nothing about the level of debt or the size of a shortfall, only about where the firm's money comes from. The bounded construction gives evenly populated, low-turnover portfolio tails, and the profitability leg enters as one of two competing funding sources rather than as a deflator, so the signal cannot reduce to cash-based profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), add( add( sstk, dltis ), max( oancf, dp ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: CapitalMarketDependenceIndex
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dlc, ADD(sstk, dltis)), ADD(ADD(dlc, ADD(sstk, dltis)), MAX(oancf, dp))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm's total reliance on capital markets is the sum of what it must refinance and what it newly raises, judged against the cash its operations produce; firms whose survival and growth depend mostly on outside capital rather than internal cash are systematically overpriced relative to their exposure to funding conditions.
input_signals.reasoning: This unifies the two strongest independent results — maturing claims deflated by internal cash (t = −3.65) and the external-funding inflow share (t = −2.27) — into a single bounded [0,1] dependence measure, which is the functional form that has produced the most stable portfolio tails while raw multiples produce outlier-driven extremes. It is not a rank blend of the parents: it is one economically defined share, so if it beats both parents the channel is capital-market dependence rather than either refinancing or issuance alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( add( dlc, add( sstk, dltis ) ), add( add( dlc, add( sstk, dltis ) ), max( oancf, dp ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: ShortMaturityTiltWeakCash
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(dlc, MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), dp))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: It is the maturity *structure* of debt, not its quantity, that interacts with cash generation: a firm whose borrowing is concentrated at the short end and whose operations generate little cash must return to lenders precisely when it is weakest.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the debt *level* with the short-term *share* of total debt removes the leverage-quantity content that makes dlc/at partly a credit-risk proxy, so this isolates maturity composition — a genuinely different financing attribute — interacted with cash-flow weakness. It reuses the weakest-link structure that succeeded in CashBurningIssuer, where both legs pointed the same economic direction, rather than the volatility conditioner that failed.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( dlc, max( add( dltt, dlc ), dp ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: SelfFundedCashGenerator
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The long half of the economic story is the mirror image of the cash-burning issuer: firms that generate substantial operating cash and simultaneously raise essentially no outside equity or debt are self-funding cash machines whose independence from capital markets is underpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: Every long-side attempt so far has been built on payout levels, which FF5 absorbs; this instead defines strength as the *absence of external funding* alongside cash generation, and it puts the sharp tail of the weakest-link operator on the long side where the hypothesis is most specific. Because CashBurningIssuer delivered −4.3% with the sharp tail on the short side, this is the direct test of whether the same conjunction logic carries information in the opposite direction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitableSelfFundedDeleveraging
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), MAX(oancf, dp))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms that use internally generated cash to retire debt are transferring value from creditors to shareholders while reducing distress risk, and because the action is unglamorous relative to buybacks the market prices it too slowly.
input_signals.reasoning: The long side of this archive has failed whenever it was built on payout levels or cash-flow-times-payout conjunctions, so this replaces distributions with net debt retirement measured against internal cash capacity — a use of cash the archive has only ever treated as a component of net financing, never as the signal itself. Unlike the flagged R&D version there is no artificial zero mass driving the tails, since both legs are continuously distributed ranks among cash-flow reporters.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), max( oancf, dp ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: FixedCommitmentShare
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), dlc), ADD(ADD(ADD(xint, dvt), dlc), MAX(oibdp, dp))), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm's total pre-committed cash requirement is interest owed to lenders, dividends promised to shareholders, and principal falling due within the year; the share of the firm's combined commitment-plus-capacity that these claims represent measures how little discretionary cash management controls, and that encumbrance is underpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: This completes the commitment measure by adding maturing principal to the interest-plus-dividend numerator that produced t = −4.55, while using the bounded [0,1] share form that gave the archive its most stable tails and strongest slope (CapitalMarketDependenceIndex, fmb = −3.41). Because capacity is accrual operating profit rather than oancf, coverage stays near 0.12 rather than falling to 0.085, so the alpha is estimated on materially more firms than the cash-flow-based incumbents.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( add( add( xint, dvt ), dlc ), add( add( add( xint, dvt ), dlc ), max( oibdp, dp ) ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: ProfitableDebtRetirementRate
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), MAX(LAG(dltt, 1), dp))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitable firms that retire a large fraction of their outstanding long-term debt are transferring value from creditors to shareholders and removing future encumbrance; the correct scaling for a repayment decision is the debt stock it reduces, not the firm's cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs a specific diagnosed failure: ProfitableSelfFundedDeleveraging had fmb = +3.27 but a null alpha because scaling net repayment by MAX(oancf, dp) puts firms with tiny cash flow, not firms with meaningful deleveraging, in the top decile. Rescaling by lagged debt outstanding makes the leg a genuine repayment *rate* bounded by economics rather than by a noisy denominator, which should convert the existing cross-sectional slope into a tradeable spread.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), max( lag( dltt, 1 ), dp ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: UnencumberedProfitLeader
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(xint, dvt), MAX(oibdp, dp)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The long side of the encumbrance story is the firm that is both highly profitable and almost entirely free of fixed claims on that profit: its cash is fully discretionary, giving it option value in downturns that the market does not capitalise.
input_signals.reasoning: This puts the sharp weakest-link tail on the long side of the archive's best-performing channel, with both legs built from income-statement items so coverage should reach ~0.12 — roughly 40% wider than any existing positive-sign signal. It is the disciplined complement to Signal 3: if the level form works and this conjunction does not, the long-side information is in residual profit magnitude; if the conjunction works better, it is in the joint absence of claims.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( xint, dvt ), max( oibdp, dp ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CommitmentVersusTroughEarnings
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(xint, dvt), MAX(TS_MIN(oibdp, 5), dp)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes fixed commitments dangerous is not their size relative to current profit but their size relative to the profit the firm earns in a bad year; a firm whose interest and dividend obligations exceed its five-year trough operating profit has already promised cash it cannot generate under stress.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not the payout ratio in any of its published forms: the denominator is the firm's own worst realised earning power over five years, so the signal is a stress test of committed outflows rather than a distribution-generosity measure, and two firms with identical payout ratios score very differently depending on the depth of their earnings cycle. It targets the specific weakness of the archive's best signal — a weak cross-sectional slope (fmb = −1.67) despite a strong alpha — by replacing current profit with the downside capacity that should determine when the commitment actually binds.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( add( xint, dvt ), max( ts_min( oibdp, 5 ), dp ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: StressTestedDiscretionaryProfit
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_MIN(SUB(oibdp, ADD(xint, dvt)), 5), at), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: The durable long-side characteristic is profit that remains discretionary even in the firm's worst year: if operating profit net of interest and dividends stayed comfortably positive throughout a five-year window, the firm has unencumbered internal funding through the cycle and its resilience is underpriced.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the flagged current-year residual — which is close to the Fama–French operating profitability definition and would be absorbed by RMW — a five-year time-series minimum measures downside profitability net of claims, a distinct characteristic that no static profitability factor spans and that cannot be constructed from either theme alone. It also addresses the diagnosed instability of the archive's positive-sign signals: a trough statistic changes slowly, so portfolio membership is persistent and the alpha should be estimated with far less turnover noise.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ts_min( sub( oibdp, add( xint, dvt ) ), 5 ), at ), 1 )

input_signals.name: DurableProfitLowEncumbrance
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(xint, dvt), MAX(oibdp, dp)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The strongest long-side case is a firm that stayed profitable even in its worst year of the last five and carries almost no fixed claims on that profit: its internal funding is both durable and unencumbered, giving it optionality that the market does not capitalise.
input_signals.reasoning: UnencumberedProfitLeader is the archive's only reliable long-side signal (+3.3%, t = +3.46), and its weakness per the critic is that a three-year average profitability leg is close to RMW; replacing it with a five-year trough profitability makes the leg a downside-persistence characteristic that no static profitability factor spans, while keeping the weakest-link structure that has proven necessary on the long side. Coverage should remain near 0.12, well above every low-coverage long-side attempt earlier in the run.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( xint, dvt ), max( oibdp, dp ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PeakCommitmentVersusCurrentProfit
input_signals.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(TS_MAX(ADD(xint, dvt), 5), MAX(oibdp, dp)), 1)
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms manage to the highest commitment level they have previously sustained — the dividend they once paid and the interest bill they once carried set the standard management defends — so the peak of the last five years of fixed outflows, measured against *today's* operating profit, identifies firms whose established obligations have outgrown their current earning power.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the leverage-ratio collapse the critic identified because the numerator remains a flow of committed outflows rather than a debt stock, but it introduces a genuinely new object: the mismatch between a historically anchored commitment level and current capacity, which no static burden ratio or credit metric expresses. It also targets the specific population where the mechanism should be strongest — firms whose profit has fallen back toward obligations they have not yet renegotiated — while keeping income-statement-only coverage near 0.12.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: winsor( ratio( ts_max( add( xint, dvt ), 5 ), max( oibdp, dp ) ), 1 )

input_signals.name: ProfitableWithTroughSafeCommitments
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(xint, dvt), MAX(TS_MIN(oibdp, 5), dp)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The durable long-side characteristic is high current profitability combined with fixed claims that are small even relative to the firm's worst recent year of earnings; such firms retain full discretion over their cash in every state of the world.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the internal tension the critic identified — no leg now requires a large dividend while another requires small commitments — and instead upgrades the encumbrance leg of the archive's best long-side signal from current to trough capacity, the same substitution that produced a −4.50 t-statistic on the short side. The two legs remain economically distinct (profit level versus stress-case claim coverage), so the intersection is a broad, stable population rather than the thin corner created by three competing conditions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( xint, dvt ), max( ts_min( oibdp, 5 ), dp ) ) ) ) )
